newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent called 5-10 cents off, gas oil down $0.5.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent called 5-10 cents off, gas oil down $0.5.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were called to open 5-10 cents lower on Friday, with gas oil 50 cents down, but the market was expected to trade low volume in narrow ranges in the absence of any Iraq news overnight, brokers said.
"There was no news overnight. It's looking very quiet today," one broker said.
September Brent settled four cents higher on Thursday, in the middle of the day's range, at $18.44 a barrel, becalmed after no fresh news emerged about Iraqi oil exports.
IPE gas oil settled unchanged on the day at $165.25 a tonne, after trading in a narrow one dollar range.
Nymex September crude futures trading on ACCESS were last done at $19.72, five cents below the pit trade settle at $19.77 after NYMEX crude firmed 10 cents on the back of a rally in August gasoline.
Iraqi oil sales under a U.N. oil-for-food deal have been delayed while the U.N. considers Baghdad's aid distribution plan.

The $2 billion six-month deal which came into effect on June 8 has been split into two three-month, $1 billion tranches and members of the U.N. sanctions committee said on Thursday Baghdad would not be allowed to change deadlines for the first tranche.
Baghdad will also not be allowed to carry over more than five percent of its oil allocation from the first tranche into the second, the U.N. has said.

Industry analysts suggest this means Iraq will have to squeeze out 1.5-2 million barrels per day when exports resume, possibly in mid-August, in order to meet its $1 billion cash target by early September.
